newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The government has set May 15 the deadline to turn Dhaka a neat and clean capital city.

The Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) has appointed former U.S. Congressman Stephen Solarz as a lobbyist to reprsent the interest of the Bangladesh ready-made garments sector in the United States.

At least 60 people, including teachers, students and police, were injured in a university campus in northern Rajshahi district on Saturday as armed student activists of fundamentalist Jamaat e Islami went bersek protsting new admission rule.

Mahbubul Haq, President of the Islamabad-based Human Development Centre, has proposed a regional advisory board comprising key intellectuals of South Asia to draw action plans on human development issues.
Rebel leaders of Jatiya Party of former military ruler Hussain Muhammad Ershad said on Saturday they would soon convene the party council.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Saturday said the livestock policy would be recast, and asked concerned authorities to put forward recommendations.
Paragon Leather and Footwear Industries Ltd, which recently offered shares, received over Tk 360 million against subscription for public issue of ordinary shares valued at Tk 30 million
Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed on Saturday asked the State Owned Enterprises (SOEs) to cut overhead expenditures.
